narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Partly cloudy conditions ahead give way to overcast skies by evening, with a high reaching 29°C (84°F) and a low of 20°C (68°F). thunder possible, peaking this evening. Showers and thunderstorms onset from 16:00 bringing 2.8 mm (0.11 in) of rain with a 78% chance. Winds are northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, gusting up to 35 km/h (19 kt). The UV index peaks at 9 today. Ground stations show air quality reaching AQI 70 at Dunga Beach. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C (73°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 7 km/h (4 kt); sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Mostly cloudy skies persist through the week. On Saturday, four of four models wet with thunder likely and highs of 28–30°C (82–86°F). Sunday brings high temperatures of 29–31°C (84–88°F) with four of four models wet and thunder likely. Monday sees four of four models wet with thunder likely, a 100% rain call, and highs of 29–30°C (84–86°F). Tuesday has four of four models wet with thunder likely. Wednesday sees two of four models wet with thunder likely, while Thursday has two of three models wet with thunder likely. Friday concludes with two of two models wet, thunder possible, a 100% rain call, and highs of 28–29°C (82–84°F).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values indicate thunderstorm potential this evening, peaking at 19:00. Best Match reaches 1790 J/kg, ECMWF reaches 2250 J/kg, ICON reaches 1500 J/kg, and UKMO reaches 4580 J/kg, all exceeding the thunderstorm threshold, while GFS remains lower at 790 J/kg. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No official warning has been issued by the met service.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Over Winam Gulf, winds move east-northeasterly overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt) gusting 10 km/h (6 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 8 km/h (4 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), then into the evening at 10 km/h (5 kt) gusting 16 km/h (9 kt); peak gust 26 km/h (14 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, sudden gusts well above the forecast wind present a hazard.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1017 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure overhead is falling. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1014.1 and 1016.4 hPa; falling by 1.6 hPa over three days. Today's call shows a pressure trend of +0.4 hPa with a moderate large-scale gradient and lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, GFS holds the best rain record at 90% accuracy over recent checks, yet no model is1 meaningfully better overall across 69 checks. GFS predicts no rain today with a 29.9°C (85.8°F) high, sitting contrary to the rain call and its own record, consistent with findings that GFS often misses thunderstorms here. ECMWF forecasts 5.1 mm (0.20 in) of rain and a high of 27.8°C (82.0°F), while ICON predicts 6 mm (0.24 in) and a 28.6°C (83.5°F) high. Best Match calls 1.1 mm (0.04 in) with a 28.9°C (84.0°F) high, and UKMO predicts 0.6 mm (0.02 in) with a 29.4°C (84.9°F) high. ECMWF and Best Match systematically or slightly under-forecast peak wind and daytime highs. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) predicts light showers and thunderstorms with a high of 28°C (82°F) and low of 20°C (68°F), agreeing with the rain call. Forecast verification is based on a settled sample of up to 95 checks per model at Day+0, 31 checks at Day+3, and 89 at Day+7, though Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) has fewer stored checks.
